LESSON: DATA SAFETY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Data Safety
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Data Safety, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How is data protected in an electronic device?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to data safety in the environment

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Data Safety in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. outline the importance of data in an electronic device, ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print media and digital devices to list, fingerspell and sign key terms used in data safety. (Viruses, hacking, cyber security passwords, scanning, data, electronic devices, antivirus) How is data protected in an electronic device? 6 c) explain threats to data in an electronic device, d) describe ways of protecting data in an electronic device, e) secure data in an electronic device, f) acknowledge the need for data safety in day-to-day life. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use personal experiences and testimonies to discuss importance of data in an electronic device and present to plenary. ● In groups, learners are guided to brainstorm on the meaning of data and information in an electronic device. ● learners are guided to discuss and make notes on the meaning of data and information in an electronic device. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use available resources to search for the importance of data in electronic devices. ● learners are guided to discuss and make notes on the importance of data in an electronic device. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print and nonprint media to search for information on threats to data 7 in electronic devices (virus and unauthorised access). ● In groups, learners are guided to discuss threats to data in electronic devices (virus and unauthorised access). ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to use digital devices to watch captioned video clips on how to prevent threats of electronic data. In cases where videos are not captioned, ensure the videos are supported by sign language interpretation and pause to allow the learner ample time to follow and interpret the videos. Probe with questions to elicit response and enhance comprehension. ● In pairs, learners are guided to use print and non-print media to search for ways of securing data stored in a computer. ● In groups, learners are guided to discuss techniques of 8 securing data in an electronic device (use passwords; and scan electronic devices using antivirus ) . ● In pairs, learners are guided to discuss ways of securing data stored in a computer. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Data Safety together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
9

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires active listening and communication skills when discussing threats

to data in electronic devices

● Digital Literacy: learner acquires skills of interacting with technology when using digital devices to secure electronic data

in a user environment

Values:
● Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when securing electronic data in the workplace against

possible threats.

● Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when brainstorming on the threats of electronic data in the work

environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cyber Security: learner enhances online safety when practising how to secure electronic data in the user environment.

Link to other subjects:

Mathematics: learner relates data safety to data handling in mathematics.
